newsitem.title: FRANCE: Promodes soars on results, merger talk.
newsitem.headline: Promodes soars on results, merger talk.

text.p: Shares in retailer Promodes jumped almost six percent on Friday, after 1996 profit figures judged by the market as "excellent", traders said.
Promodes, which operates the Continent hypermarket chain, was up 5.9 percent at 1,886 francs at 1050 GMT, after posting net attributable profit up 22 percent at 1.25 billion francs.

"We rate it a stock to buy," said a French broker, who added that the results showed strong performance in the core domestic market and net profit was much higher than the market consensus. There was still market speculation about a merger between Promodes and Casino, she added.
Casino outperformed the market, edging up 0.04 percent to 276.10 francs while the market was down 0.41 percent.

The market has long speculated about a merger between Casino and Promodes as part of an industry restructuring, with talk of a share swap on the basis of one Promodes share for six Casino, the broker said. If the terms were lower than that, it would be less advantageous for Promodes, she added.
The rise in Casino stock was smaller, as a lot of the gains had already taken place, while Promodes was staging a catch-up.

A salesman at a second French broker said changes in French law to protect city centre small retailers have curbed new large store openings at edge-of-town sites and banned the pricing of loss-leaders on 3,000 items, used to attract shoppers.
That has served to boost Casino's margins and turnover in January and February and the group is "recovering on a net margin basis," he said.

Broker Oddo revised upwards its Casino earnings estimate to 9.6 francs from 9.5 for 1996, 11.1 francs for 1997 versus 10.9, and 13 francs from 12 for 1998. It upgraded the stock to "2", or overweight, from "3", or underweight.

Casino chairman Georges Plassat told Reuters on Thursday he expected 1997 profit growth around 22.2 percent, the historic average of the last five years and to be free of debt by 1999. He declined to comment on talk of a Promodes merger.
